findings.title: Procedure omits the required summary toggle and reopen transitions
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:11-13 declares open-help by Enter, toggle-help from help-open to help-closed by Space, and reopen-help by Enter; :18 includes help-toggle among required_checks. target/verification-protocol.md:7-8 opens help through the summary with no activation specified, then immediately traverses to Close and activates Enter. None of target lines 5-10 performs Space on summary or reopens help. checks/check_contract.py:37-43 returns the supplied required_checks list, and the local checker output in /workspace/output/roles/correctness/contract-check.json includes help-toggle (exit 0), while expressly limiting that result to contract consistency. Trigger: execute the written procedure on a surface where Close and Back work but Space on summary does not close help. Every written assertion can succeed without exercising that broken transition. Impact: the procedure cannot establish the required help-toggle behavior or the declared keyboard summary sequence.

findings.title: Procedure does not establish the required request-method and origin policies
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:5-6 restricts origins to https://qaizen.io and methods to GET, HEAD, OPTIONS; :18 requires read-only-policy and origin-policy checks; :20 expects an analytics POST to be blocked and its observed effects retained. observation-policy.json:2-4 independently supplies the same origin allowlist. checks/check_contract.py:12-18 validates declared entry origin and method policy and :37-43 echoes required checks with the explicit contract-consistency-only limit. target/verification-protocol.md:5 begins by opening the public entry, but the complete six-step procedure at :5-10 supplies no origin/method enforcement, request observation, policy assertions, or blocked-analytics effects record. Trigger: follow those steps in an ordinary unrestricted browsing context that attempts the expected analytics POST. The written checks neither block nor record it and can all pass regardless of those policy obligations; likewise they do not constrain any redirect or auxiliary request to allowed origins. Impact: completion of this procedure supplies no evidence of the required policy checks and does not ensure observation stays within the declared read-only/origin scope.

findings.title: Procedure omits the required origin and read-only network controls
findings.evidence: /workspace/worker/target/verification-protocol.md:5-10 contains the entire executable procedure: navigation, unanswered state, help, Close and Back assertions, but no network-policy setup, allowed-origin check, method restriction, or blocked-request observation. /workspace/worker/surface-contract.json:5-6 allows only https://qaizen.io and GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; :18 explicitly requires read-only-policy and origin-policy checks; :20 says an analytics POST is expected to be blocked and its observed effects retained. /workspace/worker/observation-policy.json:2-4 independently limits allowed_origins to https://qaizen.io. Concrete trigger: execute the six written steps in a browser without an independently installed request filter, while navigation or a control attempts the analytics POST anticipated by contract line 20, or follows a redirect to an unauthorized origin. Every written UI assertion can pass without either required policy being established or the prohibited request being recorded. Impact: the procedure can produce an apparently successful UI trace despite unverified observation authorization and potential disallowed network side effects. This is a demonstrated omission in the procedure, not an observation of emitted traffic or a deployment defect. Static reproduction is saved in /workspace/output/roles/security/static-policy-trace.json; the actual contract checker returned valid=true with limit=Contract consistency only; browser observations establish current behavior. (/workspace/output/roles/security/contract-check.json).
